title: Quantile-aware arrival fuzzing harness for continuous batching and queueing
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Objective: build a reproducible harness that stresses continuous batching + queueing interactions under mixed workloads while surfacing quantile (p50/p90/p95/p99) drift and tokens/sec throughput regressions. The harness will generate session-aware arrival patterns, inject KV-cache hit/miss correlations, and fuzz timing to simulate real multi-tenant burstiness and tail amplification. This ticket covers design, implementation, baseline runs, and integration with the regression-detection pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay at least three canonical arrival profiles (steady, bimodal burst, heavy-tail session churn) with parameterized knobs.
Collected metrics include tokens/sec, p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, request queue depth over time, batch sizes distribution, KV cache hit rate, and per-priority-class tail amplification.
Regression detection runs on new baselines and emits alerts when p95 increases >10% or tokens/sec drops >8% relative to baseline.
Automated artifacts: summary CSV, latency heatmap PNG, and dashboard link for each run are uploaded to the benchmarking S3 folder and referenced in the ticket.
Benchmark run time for a standard profile (30 minutes simulated) completes within CI resource limits and produces deterministic seedable outputs for diffing.
steps: Design arrival generator API (session-level, burst probability, priority tags, KV-hit correlation parameter)
Implement generator as a standalone binary (go) and a python harness wrapper for experiment orchestration
Wire runtime metrics export: per-req latency, batch size histogram, queue depth, KV cache stats; ensure consistent tagging
Create baseline profiles and run them on staging runtime-1.23 image to capture baseline artifact set
Integrate artifact uploader and result summary into regression detector so CI can compare new runs against baseline
Create Grafana dashboard and a static summary report template for PRs/exec review
testbed_config: Staging cluster: 4x A100-like instances behind the multi-tenant runtime image runtime-1.23
Traffic generator run from dedicated bench host with controlled CPU cap to avoid generator-side jitter
Seeded RNGs for arrival generator and request payloads (seed specified in run metadata)
KV cache configured with 20% synthetic prefix reuse for mixed workload profiles
Profiles: steady(60rps, 95% short sessions), bimodal-burst(50rps+500rps microbursts), churn-heavy(large number of short-lived sessions with high cold-KV rate)
results_summary: Initial baseline (2026-02-15) on runtime-1.23: steady profile tokens/sec 120k, p95 42ms; bimodal-burst p95 148ms with 17% tokens/sec drop during microbursts; churn-heavy produced highest tail amplification index (3.4)
Regression detector configured and tested: alert threshold p95 +10% and tokens/sec -8% triggered correctly on synthetic degraded run (injected 30% slower kernel path)
Observed sensitivity: small increases in queueing delay (5ms average) amplified p95 by >25% in bimodal-burst profile due to batching alignment shifts

Preliminary conclusion: KV-hit correlation significantly reduces tail amplification in churn-heavy runs; recommending prioritizing prefix cache improvements and batch formation heuristics for customer workloads with short lived sessions.
decisions: Use seedable arrival fuzzing rather than purely replay traces to allow combinatorial sweeps across parameter space while maintaining reproducibility
Collect both request-to-first-token and end-to-end latencies to separate runtime batching effects from downstream tokenization/IO variability
Keep generator CPU-light and limit concurrent generator threads to prevent generator CPU from dominating tail behavior
Expose 'priority class' tag on each synthetic request to model platform routing policies and study priority inversion effects
blockers: Need an endpoint to export per-request KV-cache annotations from the runtime (PR open: github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/2140 awaiting review)
Staging quota on A100-like instances is currently limited during this cycle; experiment schedule may slip if additional capacity is not provisioned
Regression pipeline requires a compact binary diff format for baselines; design doc pending (see link below)
